articles.title: Transcriptional and DNA Methylation Changes in the Hippocampus and Prefrontal Cortex after Fractionated Cranial Radiation in Mice
articles.content: Fractionated whole-brain irradiation is essential for treating brain tumors, but many long-term survivors develop cognitive decline whose molecular basis is poorly understood. We asked which cell types and gene programs change late after irradiation, how the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex compare, and whether DNA methylation changes affect the same genes or programs. Male and female mice received whole-brain irradiation (5 x 4 Gy) or anesthesia alone. Irradiated mice showed persistent deficits in executive function and spatial memory. Eleven weeks after irradiation, single-nucleus RNA sequencing and whole-genome bisulfite sequencing of pooled hippocampal (CA1-3) and prefrontal tissue showed cell-type-specific transcriptional changes in neurons of both regions. Both regions showed reduced ribosomal-protein gene expression and changes in adhesion genes, with reduced respiratory-chain genes in prefrontal neurons and bidirectional synaptic gene changes in hippocampus. Differentially methylated regions were enriched at promoters, with hypermethylation predominating in three of the four sex-by-region contrasts. Methylation and gene expression changes pointed to overlapping synaptic and signaling programs, largely through different genes.
articles.author: Aksoy, T., Sumazin, P., Lu, Y., Najaf Panah, M. J., Zamorano, M., Lam, T., Zhou, W., Veselinovic, I., Duman, J. G., Gaber, M. W., Heijnen, C. J., Grosshans, D. R.

articles.title: A common neural axis links image distinctiveness and memorability
articles.content: Stimulus-specific memorability, the tendency for people to remember and forget the same stimuli, is a powerful predictor of memory performance that is independent of the study and retrieval factors that have dominated memory research. Critically, memorability can be defined in two ways: "Hit-ability" (H-ability) and "false alarm-ability" (FA-ability), the probability of correctly recognizing studied items or falsely recognizing unstudied items, respectively. Although past work has suggested that these are dissociable facets of memorability, challenging single-factor explanations, we present neural and computational evidence that they share a common neural axis. The neural signature of high H-ability matched the signature for low FA-ability, showing that these parameters have inverse relationships with a common factor. Moreover, we show that image distinctiveness predicts the flipped relationship between H-ability and FA-ability in both behavior and neural activity, providing a unifying explanation of stimulus-specific memorability.
articles.author: Utochkin, I., Chang, W., Vogel, E. K., Awh, E.

articles.title: Neuropathological assessment of cerebrovascular integrity in Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy
articles.content: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy neuropathological change (CTE-NC) is defined by perivascular deposits of phosphorylated tau, with lesions preferentially located at sulcal depths. We investigated whether CTE-NC is associated with structural changes to perivascular spaces (PVSs) or microvascular degeneration. Post-mortem middle frontal gyrus tissue from 11 CTE-NC cases and 11 age-matched controls was examined using immunohistochemistry. All CTE-NC cases exhibited pathognomonic lesions in this region. We quantified PVS width along with vessel lumen and PVS area, string vessel burden, pericyte density, and aquaporin-4 (AQP4) polarisation to the astrocytic endfoot. Total PVS width did not differ significantly between the groups in grey matter (P = 0.543) nor white matter (P = 0.468). Neither PVS area (sulcal depth, P = 0.097; gyral crest, P = 0.645) nor PVS-to-lumen area ratio (sulcal depth, P = 0.454; gyral crest, P = 0.307) differed significantly. Similarly, there were no significant differences in total microvascular length (p = 0.693), string vessel burden (p = 0.128), pericyte density (p = 0.589), or AQP4 endfoot enrichment (p = 0.538). We therefore found no evidence of large-scale PVS enlargement, lumen narrowing, capillary degeneration, pericyte loss, or altered AQP4 endfoot enrichment in CTE-NC at the locations and spatial scales investigated. Taken together, these findings suggest that the pathognomonic perivascular tau lesion is not associated with a classical small vessel degenerative phenotype in CTE-NC. However, that does not exclude more subtle molecular, functional, or ultrastructural changes at the interface between vessels, the perivascular space, and surrounding brain tissue.
articles.author: Martinac, A. E., DeLorenzo, A., Dik, D., Pasas, L., Bilston, L. E., Shepherd, C. E.

articles.title: Distinct input-output relationships between basal forebrain subnuclei underlie heterogeneous cholinergic modulation of the mouse cortex
articles.content: The basal forebrain (BF) supports many behavioral functions via its brain-wide projections, which can be recruited independently and task specifically. However, the anatomical underpinnings for this functional heterogeneity are poorly understood. Here, we compared two mouse BF subnuclei, the horizontal diagonal band (HDB) and the substantial innominata (SI), in terms of their anatomical connectivity and functional recruitment. Using anterograde and retrograde tracing, we show that they target largely segregated forebrain regions, but their input comes from a partially overlapping subset of regions. However, many neurons within each region project to just one of the subnuclei, suggesting they can be recruited independently. To test this, we combined optogenetics and widefield Ca2+ imaging and showed that stimulating prefrontal cortical projections to the HDB or SI results in distinct large-scale patterns of cortical activity via a cholinergic mechanism. Our results provide an anatomical basis for the flexible, area-specific cholinergic modulation of brain function.
articles.author: Pinto, L., Tan, J., Harter, A. M., Kolb, M., Lu, R.

articles.title: Striatal dopamine availability peaks in adulthood and undergoes age-dependent modulation
articles.content: Age is a risk factor for several psychiatric disorders. An adolescent peak in striatal dopamine availability is thought to contribute to the neuropsychiatric vulnerability. However, the lifespan trajectory of striatal dopamine release capacity is undefined in most species. Here, we measured lifespan trajectories of striatal dopamine in primates and rodents and identified a delayed developmental peak in adulthood and age-dependent changes in dopamine release regulation by GABA and acetylcholine across species.

articles.title: Advanced meditation stabilizes cortical dynamics through inhibitory gain control linked to absorptive depth
articles.content: Advanced meditation can shift conscious experience from ordinary body- and world-centered awareness toward absorption, detachment and dissociation-like states, yet the neural mechanisms that stabilize these immersive states remain unclear. We studied 18 long-term meditators during eyes-open rest and Rajyoga meditation, a practice in which practitioners reduce bodily identification while enhancing inner self-awareness. We combined multidimensional neural approach including frontal EEG spectral power, temporal non-stationarity and corticothalamic neural-field modeling, because these measures probe underlying complementary levels of the brain state transition: the strength of neural activity, its temporal stability, and the circuit level inhibition-excitation gain mechanisms. This framework is especially relevant to meditation because oscillatory, temporal organization may distinguish stable meditative states, and corticothalamic dynamics are closely linked to arousal and conscious state regulation. We correlated meditation induced neural changes with subjective ratings of absorption and dissociation. Compared with rest, meditation was associated with higher beta1, beta2 and gamma power, with no change in the slower bands (delta, theta and alpha), and with lower beta-band temporal non-stationarity, indicating a more stable expression of fast cortical dynamics. Fitting the corticothalamic model to the EEG spectra showed stronger cortical inhibitory gain and lower effective intracortical gain, placing meditation in an inhibition-dominant regime, with lower gain in the loop between excitatory and inhibitory neurons within the cortex. During meditation, these model estimates were related to subjective absorption and showed trend level links with dissociation. Together, these findings suggest that Rajyoga meditation stabilizes cortical dynamics through inhibitory gain control, linking absorption (deep and steady attention on the meditation) to dissociation-like self-detachment.
articles.author: Panda, R., Kumar, G., Nunez, P., Subramaniam, B., Bhandare, K., Malipeddi, S., Major, G., Gosseries, O., Laureys, S., Tewarie, P.

articles.title: Learned associations constrain anticipatory visual dynamics and enhance sensory and motor readiness to facilitate perceptual decisions
articles.content: Learned cue target associations can guide attention to facilitate perceptual decision making, yet how they shape the content and dynamics of neural activity, and whether this facilitation reflects anticipatory preparation, post-target sensory enhancement, or both, remains unclear. Here, we used magnetoencephalography while participants made living/nonliving judgments about visual objects (e.g., cat/violin) with left- or right-hand button presses. Cue category associations were established through repeated pairings: predictive cues always preceded one target category, whereas uninformative cues preceded both categories equally often. Predictive cues facilitated behavioral responses despite limited explicit awareness of the learned associations. Representational similarity analysis showed that prediction preactivated target-specific representations in the visual cortex resembling target evoked activity before target onset. Prediction also elicited anticipatory, response specific motor beta suppression. Together, these findings supported anticipatory preparation, with little evidence of enhanced posttarget visual specificity. Posttarget visual specificity and anticipatory motor preparation independently predicted response speed, with hierarchical drift diffusion modeling linking greater visual specificity to faster evidence accumulation and stronger motor preparation to shorter nondecision time (a model parameter reflecting sensory encoding and motor execution). Beyond representational content, prediction also constrained the evolution of anticipatory visual population activity, and more constrained, stable early visual trajectories predicted faster responses. These population dynamics were associated with faster evidence accumulation, lower decision thresholds, and shorter non-decision time. Together, these findings suggest that associative memory facilitates perceptual decisions by shaping the content and dynamics of anticipatory neural activity, with partially dissociable contributions from visual processing and motor preparation.
articles.author: Zhang, L., Yuan, M., Zhang, H., Morris Moscovitch, M., Alain, C.

articles.title: Tri-Modal Single-Cell Atlas of Developing Human Brain
articles.content: Epigenetic modifications, such as DNA methylation, evolve throughout development and aging, providing remarkable regulatory diversity and contributing to disease etiology, including neuropsychiatric disorders. However, how these regulatory layers interact across human brain development remains unclear. Leveraging ME-seq, we simultaneously mapped gene expression, chromatin accessibility, and DNA methylation in over 340,000 single nuclei from 40 human brain specimens spanning fetal development to adolescence. Chromatin accessibility and DNA methylation captured partially overlapping cis-regulatory associations. Developmental trajectories revealed distinct temporal kinetics: DNA methylation continued remodeling beyond major transcriptional and accessibility transitions, while developmental clocks yielded modality-dependent age estimates. Modality-specific regulatory networks converged on developmental transcription factors, whereas methylation-defined regulatory regions provided complementary annotations of neuropsychiatric genetic risk. Together, these findings establish DNA methylation as a persistent and complementary dimension of developmental regulation, linking prolonged remodeling to human brain maturation and disease susceptibility.
articles.author: Song, L., Wang, Z., Zhu, B., DeKuyper, F. A., Wang, C., Liao, Z., Girdhar, K., Lee, D., Tsankova, N. M., Kaji, D. A., Fullard, J. F., Dong, P., Roussos, P., Ma, S.

articles.title: Hyperglycemia-responsive circRNA drives diabetic neuropathic pain by competing for PUM2 binding and promoting proNT3/CCL2 in DRG neurons
articles.content: Diabetic neuropathic pain (DNP), one of the most common and debilitating complications of diabetes mellitus (DM), remains poorly managed by conventional analgesics, highlighting the urgent need to explore its etiology-associated mechanisms. Here, we identified a novel conserved circular RNA, cRps6kb1, that is significantly upregulated in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons across multiple mouse models of type 1 DM and type 2 DM, as well as in human donors with DNP. Blocking cRps6kb1 upregulation attenuated the increases in DRG neurotrophin-3 mRNA (Nt3), its encoded proneurotrophin-3 (proNT3), and downstream C-C chemokine ligand 2 (CCL2) expression, as well as the persistence of nociceptive hypersensitivity under the conditions of streptozotocin-induced type 1 DM or high-fat diet-fed type 2 DM. Conversely, mimicking cRps6kb1 upregulation increased DRG Nt3, proNT3, and CCL2 levels and produced DNP-like symptoms in naive mice. In addition, high glucose increased the expression of cRps6kb1 and Nt3 in cultured DRG neurons from mice and human donors. Mechanistically, upregulated cRps6kb1 competed with the Nt3 3'-untranslated region (3-UTR) for the translational repressor PUM2 binding, releasing PUM2 from the Nt3 3-UTR and enhancing Nt3 mRNA translation and stability. Thus, cRps6kb1 is a key contributor to DNP and represents a promising therapeutic target for its treatment.
articles.author: Li, X., Huang, C., Govindarajalu, G., Wang, B., Zhang, H.-H., Feng, X., Sharma, D., Ma, R., Zhang, L., Zheng, B., Xiao, J., Ferreira, M. d. A., Berkman, T., Cabrera, J., Li, X., Jiang, B.-C., Zhang, X.-S., Davidson, S., TAO, Y.-X.

articles.title: A novel behavioral paradigm for characterizing anticipatory postural adjustments in mice
articles.content: Voluntary movements perturb the body's equilibrium, and the nervous system limits this disturbance by generating anticipatory postural adjustments (APAs) that redistribute body weight before and during movement. APAs have been characterized extensively in humans and larger animal models, but the absence of a tractable behavioral assay in mice has limited access to the genetic and circuit-level tools needed to investigate their neural basis. Here, we describe a force-plate behavioral paradigm in which freely moving mice stand on four independent load cells, receive an auditory GO cue and initiate locomotion voluntarily without task-specific training. Using force recordings, high-speed video and markerless pose estimation, we show that mice initiate a step with a stereotyped sequence of weight shifts: the center of pressure (CoP) moves anteriorly and then laterally away from the swing side, the swing forepaw and diagonally opposite hindpaw unload, and body weight is carried by the remaining diagonal pair. A single principal component explained approximately 80% of the variance in the average trial, compared with approximately 50% when paw identity was shuffled. Pressure recordings identified rapid swing-forepaw unloading beginning, on average, 87.9 ms before lift-off. Head and ear movement began approximately 200 ms before lift-off, and an operational multimodal estimate placed the interval between the earliest detected postural movement and the onset of forepaw rotation at approximately 160-180 ms. Neuropixels recordings from the pontine reticular nucleus (PRN) and supplementary motor area (SMA), monosynaptic tracing of inputs to reticulospinal PRN neurons, and preliminary cell-ablation experiments identify the PRN as a candidate node in the circuitry supporting anticipatory postural control. This paradigm provides a platform for circuit-level investigation of postural control and its disruption in disease.

articles.title: Meditation as a bioactive intervention: evidence of translational potential via Connectivity Mapping and TMS neurophysiology
articles.content: BackgroundMeditation practices are often used as non-pharmacological adjunct therapy for managing stress and wellbeing benefits. Here, we investigate whether molecular signatures via meditation practices have potential overlap with those of known drug targets that have established neurophysiological relevance.MethodWe leverage the Connectivity Map (CMap) to investigate (a) the overlap between meditation-induced molecular signatures and established drug responses, and (b) the pathways and mechanisms contributing to meditation’s potential therapeutic effects. This was studied in a comprehensive temporal RNAseq dataset comprising premeditation, meditation, and follow-up stages from a clinical trial involving 106 participants practizing inner engineering meditation. With Multiple Correspondence Analysis (MCA), we then examined how overlapping neuroactive drug classes identified from a systematic-literature search derived pharmaco-Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) responses and CMap results co-occurred within a shared latent space.ResultsMeditation associated signatures overlapped with over 438 drugs, but predominantly with drugs targeting the neuroactive ligand interaction receptor pathways, capable of modulating the brain’s excitation-inhibition (E/I) balance. We found that meditation associated transcriptome signatures showed connectivity with drugs targeting the GABA, glutamine and other neuromodulatory system pathways. This pattern was further corroborated by Multiple Correspondence Analysis (MCA) of drugs from pharmaco-TMS studies and CMap, which revealed distinct temporal patterns of these drug classes across meditation stages.ConclusionThis integrative approach offers a molecular lens to view meditation’s potential neurophysiological effects. Rather than establishing causal mechanisms, our findings are intended to generate hypotheses: how meditation-associated molecular pathway changes might relate to shifts in E/I balance. We propose a working model to test these associations directly using neurophysiological measures, with the eventual goal of informing evidence-based clinical applications. Overall, these exploratory findings have increased the potential possibility to correlate meditation with biologically relevant molecular and neurophysiological correlates, hence, providing an additional dimension to meditation’s currently established characterization as a psychological and contemplative practice.
articles.author: Mitali Mukerji

articles.title: Hearing loss as an inference problem: sensory precision, conversational repair, and partner adaptation
articles.content: Conversational understanding is often approached as a problem of successful signal transmission. This paper develops a complementary account in which conversation is treated as a reciprocal process of inference and action: interlocutors must infer the latent causes of one another’s signals, estimate the reliability of the available evidence, and act to keep uncertainty sufficiently manageable for coordinated exchange. Hearing loss provides a theoretically revealing case for understanding conversation as reciprocal inference because it perturbs the generative process through which speech causes produce auditory observations, while also increasing the importance of contextual inference, precision control, conversational repair, and partner adaptation. We develop an active inference framework with three principal contributions. First, we distinguish the sensory perturbation produced by hearing loss from the listener’s generative model representation of that perturbation through reduced, redistributed, or potentially miscalibrated likelihood precision. Second, we differentiate compensatory precision control, delayed commitment, covert repair, and overt conversational repair, treating overt repair as an epistemic policy whose value depends on expected information gain, prior preferences, learned policy habits, and interpersonal consequences. Third, we extend the framework beyond the isolated listener by formalising how interlocutors infer one another’s states, select partner-sensitive policies, and update partner models through repeated interaction. The proposal therefore connects foundational questions with a clinically and socially consequential sensory condition. Rather than treating hearing loss solely as an individual perceptual deficit, it examines how altered sensory evidence changes the coupled inferential dynamics through which listeners and communication partners jointly maintain understanding. The framework generates empirically discriminating predictions and outlines how these can ultimately be evaluated through model comparison, behavioural and physiological measures, dyadic interaction paradigms, and longitudinal research. Overall, the proposal recasts hearing-impaired conversation as the joint regulation of uncertainty under asymmetric sensory and interpersonal constraints.
articles.author: Sebastian Schnettler

articles.title: Noise resilience in brain decoding driven by spiking neural networks for responsive robot control
articles.content: Brain computer interface (BCI) is a promising technology, expanding on many fields ranging from medical to commercial applications. The diffusion of this technique is compromised by the complexity of the treated data and the unavoidable presence of noise in those systems. This study contributes to the solution of this problem by proposing a BCI pipeline that relies on the use of spiking neural networks (SNNs), quantifying their robustness to noise in the context of brain decoding through the classification of Electroencephalography (EEG). We benchmark a shallow convolutional network against two spiking counterparts based on leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) and adaptive LIF neurons on the four-class BNCI 2014-001 motor imagery dataset. The conventional model has a slight advantage in clean conditions, but it degrades dramatically once the input is corrupted. In contrast, SNN demonstrates remarkable robustness under signal degradation. Under global Gaussian noise, CNN accuracy drops by 58.56%, whereas Adaptive LIF SNN accuracy drops by only 0.80%. Similarly, when trained on recordings with one electrode removed and tested on the complete montage, CNN loses 36.00% of its accuracy, compared with 0.34% for the SNN. With semi-simulated ocular, muscular and cardiac artifacts the gap is smaller, but the spiking models still degrade less than the CNN for every artifact type. This robustness is obtained at equal model size with 18.0 of the 24.6 MMAC required per trial by the baseline replaced by accumulate-only, spike-driven operations. Finally, the spiking model was integrated in a full decoding-to-actuation pipeline driving a Franka Emika Research 3 robot from a replayed EEG stream. These findings indicate that, compared with a dense counterpart, spiking computation substantially reduces the sensitivity of EEG decoding to signal corruption, which supports the use of SNNs in deployments where robustness matters more than peak accuracy.
